records.name: Cosmic Writers
records.summary: A nonprofit that uses writing to help children become creative and critical thinkers. It offers free one-on-one coaching for young writers, a drop-in writing night, and classroom help for teachers.
records.what_you_do: Young writers can get free one-on-one coaching (matched to a coach who knows their genre; sign-ups reopen in January 2027), or drop in on Friday Night Writes (Fridays 4 to 6 pm, online or in person at Gutmann College House). Families can also buy a writing activity book for $9.95 and try it at home.

schedule.text: Friday Night Writes is a drop-in on Fridays from 4 to 6 pm during the fall term, online or in person. Cosmic Coaching is one session a week for eight weeks, at a time the coach and writer agree on.

locations.label: Friday Night Writes, in person (when offered)
locations.address: Gutmann College House, 211 S. 40th St., Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Cosmic Coaching is free. The page does not list a cost for Friday Night Writes.

first_step.how: Reserve a virtual slot for Friday Night Writes with the sign-up form on the Cosmic Writers site when the program is running, or go in person to Gutmann College House, 211 S. 40th St. Coaching sign-ups are closed for fall 2026 and reopen in January 2027.
first_step.basis: Friday Night Writes is a public drop-in with a simple slot reservation for virtual visits. The page does not describe a welcome for first timers. Coaching is closed until the new term.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday Night Writes runs from 4 to 6 pm on Fridays during the fall. You can get feedback on your writing, including college essays and entries for the Scholastic Art and Writing Awards. Visits happen online or in person at Gutmann College House, and the page does not give a price.
first_visit_tips: Reserve a virtual slot ahead of time with the form on the site.
Bring a piece of writing you want feedback on.
You can drop in on Friday Night Writes even if you already work with a Cosmic Coach.

records.notes: The coaching page says Spring 2026 in one section and Spring 2027 in the main notice; this record uses 2027 from the main notice. Friday Night Writes has no year printed, so the fall 2026 term is inferred from the page's Fall 2026 wording, which puts the September 25 start in 2026. kids_ok is true because the page says coaching is for young writers of all ages and the family programs are for students. The in person location (Gutmann College House, 211 S. 40th St.) is taken from the same page. The monster-building experience and the 2025 annual report are not used because they have no sign-up or date.

records.name: Dickinson Square West Civic Association
records.summary: A neighbors' association for the area between 4th and 6th Streets, from Washington Avenue to Snyder Avenue. It works on parks, cleanups, safety, and zoning, and the City consults it on local development.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come to the monthly public meeting to share ideas, raise concerns, and talk over zoning and development requests. The site lists past cleanups and block events, most recently in 2022.

schedule.text: Public meetings are held on the third Tuesday of each month, 6 to 7:30 pm. The group does not meet when the date falls on Election Day.

first_step.how: Come to the monthly public meeting on the third Tuesday, 6 to 7:30 pm, at 2219 S 7th St. Before you go, email info@dswca.org to confirm the next date, because the group's site has not been updated since 2022.
first_step.basis: The meeting page says all neighbors are welcome to attend, share ideas, and raise concerns, with no membership or dues step listed. The site was last updated in 2022, so the schedule may be out of date.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page describes the meeting as in person and does not mention Zoom. Neighbors share ideas and raise concerns, and the group talks over zoning and development requests in the area. The page does not say how long the discussion runs or how the meeting is run.
first_visit_tips: Email info@dswca.org ahead of time to confirm the date and place.
Plan to arrive a little before 6 pm.
Bring any questions about a nearby project or zoning request.

records.notes: Dormant on purpose: the group's own news page is its newest dated evidence (last post June 29, 2022), and the site says it has not been updated since spring 2022. A web search found only 2017 items. Tier 1 set active from the City RCO registry listing (dated 2026-10); a registry listing is not group activity, so it was not counted. The meeting schedule on the attend page is undated. Email replaced: tier 1 carried a personal Gmail address from the City list, and the group publishes info@dswca.org. The 2022 news lists a different meeting place (Mount Mariah Baptist Temple, 410 Wharton St), so the current place rests on the attend page alone. The get-involved page lists no volunteer roles, cleanup dates, or dues. Recommend review before this record goes live.

records.name: Dolce Suono Ensemble
records.summary: A chamber music group that puts on concerts in Philadelphia, tours, and commissions new pieces. Audiences come to the concert series, and the group also runs community partnerships.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to one of the Sunday 3 pm concerts in the home series, or follow the young composer competitions and online lecture series. Single tickets are $30 general or $10 student.

schedule.text: Home concerts are Sunday afternoons at 3 pm at Trinity at 22nd, four concerts per season. The 2026 to 2027 season has concerts in October, December, February, and June.

cost.text: Single concerts are $30 general or $10 student. A subscription to all four concerts is $120 general or $40 student.

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket for any Sunday 3 pm concert on the events page, using the PayPal link for that concert. The next one is October 11, 2026.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public and sold by ticket. The page does not mention a welcome for first timers, a newcomer event, or sales at the door.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert is a Sunday afternoon performance at Trinity at 22nd, 2212 Spruce Street, starting at 3 pm. At least one concert in June 2026 was followed by a reception. The page does not say how long a concert lasts.
first_visit_tips: Buy your ticket online ahead of time through the concert's PayPal link.
If you plan to come more than once, a subscription to all four concerts is $120 general or $40 student.

records.notes: The venue address 2212 Spruce Street comes from the events page; the tickets page gives only Spruce and 22nd. No accessibility or seating information is published, so access is omitted. drop_in is false because the only purchase route shown is advance online payment; door sales are not stated. community_band is the closest interest tag for a chamber ensemble, since no chamber music tag exists. The season changed from year_round to event_only because the concerts run October to June only. Tier 1 listed a June 14, 2026 concert; the events page now lists four 2026 to 2027 concerts.

records.name: Fairmount Civic Association
records.summary: The neighborhood group for Fairmount. It shares local news, follows zoning and development plans, and hosts community events such as Neighbors Nights and a fall stoop sale.
records.what_you_do: Members meet monthly to talk over zoning and development. Committees cover activities, crime and safety, education, neighborhood cleanups, membership, parking and transportation, and zoning. Membership dues are $15 a year for one adult.

schedule.text: General meetings are held on the last Thursday of the month. A social starts at 7 pm and the meeting at 7:30 pm, at The City School, 860 N. 24th St. The 2026 schedule has no meetings in July, August, or November.

locations.label: Monthly meeting place
locations.address: The City School, 860 N. 24th St., Philadelphia, PA 19130

cost.text: Annual dues are $15 for one adult or $20 for a household. Seniors 65 and older pay $5 alone, $10 for two seniors in a household, or $17 for a household with one senior. The site lists no free membership.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the FCA site to get the link and details for the next monthly meeting, then come to the meeting on the last Thursday at 7 pm at The City School, 860 N. 24th St.
first_step.basis: The FAQ suggests joining is the way to take part in meetings and events, and dues are $15 or more. The page does not say whether non-members can attend. The newsletter gives the meeting link, which is a clear first step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings open with a social at 7 pm, and the business meeting starts at 7:30 pm. Members can vote at monthly meetings if their membership is valid the day before. The group reviews zoning and development plans in the area, and the page does not say whether a non-member can speak.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter first, since meeting links go to subscribers.
Pay dues by the day before a meeting if you want to vote there; paying at the meeting does not make you eligible for that meeting.
Arrive by 7 pm if you want the social before the business meeting.

records.notes: The membership page does not say who may join (residency is not stated). The membership page and the FAQ both leave open whether non-members can attend, so newcomer friendliness is 2. The FAQ says meeting links go to newsletter subscribers. Email changed from zoning@ (City RCO list) to board@, the address the group gives for questions; zoning@ and membership@ also appear on the committees page. Status is active from the group's own news (posts dated September 3 and September 29, 2026).

records.name: Franklin Bridge North Neighbors Inc
records.summary: A resident-run neighborhood group for Old City, covering the area from the Ben Franklin Bridge north to Callowhill Street and from Letitia Street east to 6th Street. It follows zoning and planning and shares neighborhood news, with community meetings and cleanups.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors reach the group by email or its Facebook group, then come to a community meeting or neighborhood cleanup. Membership needs annual dues set by the board, and general meetings and events are open to the public.

cost.text: Membership requires annual dues set by the board. The amount is not on the site. General meetings and events are open to the public without membership.

first_step.how: Email franklinbridgenorthneighbors@gmail.com to ask for the next community meeting or cleanup, or join the group's Facebook group, where in person events are announced.
first_step.basis: The bylaws say general meetings and events are open to the public and that you do not need to be a member to attend. The site does not post meeting times, so a first timer has to ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical meeting or cleanup and does not post meeting times, so ask by email first. The bylaws require the membership and the board to meet at least once every three months, and you do not need to be a member to come.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email for the next date, time, and place before you come.
Join the Facebook group so you hear about cleanups and meetings when they are announced.

records.notes: No meeting times, and no dated activity on the group's own site except a 2021 bylaws adoption; the 2024 and 2026 copyright lines are not evidence. Tier 1 set active from the City RCO listing (dated 2026-10); a registry listing is not group activity, so status is probably_active with low confidence and last_sign_of_life is cleared. The meeting place 'Remote, via Zoom' comes only from the City list. Officer names are on the about page and were not recorded. The phone and contact name are carried from the City list; the email is published on the group's own site.

records.name: Hawthorne Empowerment Coalition
records.summary: A volunteer group for the Hawthorne neighborhood in South Philadelphia. It works on safety, zoning, parks and street trees, and youth and adult computer classes, and it holds open community meetings for neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors come to open community meetings, review nearby zoning and building proposals, and join park and street cleanups. The group also runs summer movie nights and jazz concerts in Hawthorne Park. All Hawthorne residents may join, and the site does not mention dues.

schedule.text: Open community meetings are usually on a Thursday evening at 7 pm, in most months. The meeting is at the Hawthorne Cultural Center, 1200 Carpenter St., or on Zoom, depending on the month, and the group calendar shows each month's place.

first_step.how: Come to a community meeting at the Hawthorne Cultural Center, 1200 Carpenter St., or on Zoom. Check the group calendar for the next date and place, or sign up for the mailing list on the site.
first_step.basis: Open community meetings are public and posted on the group's calendar. Joining is open to Hawthorne residents, and the site does not describe a welcome for first timers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Community meetings are held in the evening, usually at 7 pm. Recent meeting posts cover the group's work, officer changes, school and City Council issues, and board elections. The meeting is at the Hawthorne Cultural Center or on Zoom, so check which before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the calendar first, since some meetings are on Zoom and others are at the Hawthorne Cultural Center.
Bring a question about a nearby building or zoning project if you have one.
Arrive a few minutes early so you can find a seat before the meeting starts.

records.notes: Tier 1 had no schedule. The group's public calendar, linked from its site, lists 2026 community meetings, mostly Thursdays at 7 pm, some on Zoom, with the newest meeting dated September 24, 2026. The blog's newest post is from June 2025. Categories nature-environment and making-tech and interests park_cleanup, tree_tending, and digital_skills were added from the site and calendar (cleanups, street trees, and adult and children computer classes). The email zoning@ is carried from the City RCO list; the group's own email is hidden on the site. The calendar also lists Hawthorne Park summer movies and jazz nights in 2025 and 2026; they are not described as free, so no cost is stated for them.

records.name: Independence Historical Trust
records.summary: Philanthropic partner to Independence National Historical Park. It raises money for restoration and public projects, runs public talks, movie nights and tours, and uses volunteers for tours and events.
records.what_you_do: Lead free Twilight Tours in summer, help staff events such as the Pops on Independence concert, July 4 activities, and the annual meeting, or help in the office. The public can attend talks, movie nights, Halloween events, and tours.

schedule.text: Twilight Tours run every day in summer, from Memorial Day weekend to the end of September, at 5:15 pm, with a second 6 pm tour Thursday to Sunday. Talks, movie nights, and holiday events are listed by date on the events page.

locations.label: Twilight Tours meeting point
locations.address: Next to the Liberty Bell Center viewing window, across from Independence Hall, near Chestnut Street, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Twilight Tours are free. The events page does not list prices for other events, and some ask for a registration or RSVP.

first_step.how: Join a free Twilight Tour, which needs no reservation. Meet next to the Liberty Bell Center viewing window, across from Independence Hall, near Chestnut Street.
first_step.basis: Twilight Tours are free, need no reservation, and are open to visitors and locals. Volunteer roles need an email or form, and the page does not say what training is given or who may volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Twilight Tour is about an hour on foot, led by a local guide who designs the route and theme, past sites such as Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. Tours start at 5:15 pm each day, with a 6 pm tour too on Thursday to Sunday. Volunteers help lead tours, staff events, or do office work, and the page does not describe training.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes early to find the group by the Liberty Bell Center viewing window.
Check the Twilight Tours page for the current season, since the tours run only for part of the year.
To ask about volunteer roles, email attn@inht.org or call 215-861-4971.

records.notes: The contact name Friends of Indep National H came from IRS data and is a truncated organization name, not a person, so it was dropped; the group's pages name no contact person. The volunteer form fields did not show in the fetched text, so the form may need a live check. Minimum age, time commitment, training, and background checks are not stated, so they are left out. The Twilight Tours page describes a summer season each year; the 2026 season ended September 30, 2026. No accessibility statement appears on the tours page, so access is omitted.

leads_only.name: FESPP
leads_only.note: Named as a partner for the Neighbors Nights events on Fairmount Civic Association's site (July and August 2026). Only the abbreviation is written on the page; not checked.

notes: Input file: the brief named 002.json, but the batch folder holds 01.json to 94.json, so 02.json was used (the seven groups in that file). Seven records, all verdict publish. Fetches: 25 of 60 allowed, never more than 6 per group. Searches: 1 of 1; the Dickinson Square West search returned only 2017 items. No blocked pages and no rate limiting. Status changes from tier 1: Cosmic Writers from probably_active to active (fall 2026 program notices); Dickinson Square West from active to dormant (own site last posted June 2022); Franklin Bridge North from active to probably_active (no dated activity on its own site; low confidence); Hawthorne, Fairmount and Independence Historical Trust stay active with newer dates from their own sites or calendar. Contact changes: Dickinson Square West email replaced with the group's own info@dswca.org (tier 1 carried a personal Gmail from the City list); Fairmount email set to board@ (the group's stated questions address); Independence Historical Trust contact name dropped as a truncated organization name. Flagged for review: Dickinson Square West (dormant, low confidence, meeting schedule undated on its site) and Franklin Bridge North (no meeting times, low confidence).
